title: The Sessions list answers as one page

statements.says: A read of the Sessions list sends its head, then every row in one line, then its end.
The Sessions list keeps the NDJSON transport, the Arriving state and the Gap that every Events store read has.
The Sessions list drops the day-by-day split of a read.
A run is never cut at a day boundary, the midnight rule.
A store that stops answering part way leaves no rows at all, and the answer carries an unreachable Gap naming every day of the span.
An answer that fell short is told apart from one that found nothing by the row line: absent means still reading, and a line with no rows means the period was quiet.
The Sessions list is a list of runs, and a run is not a day: a Session that began before midnight and ended after it belongs to no single day.
Cutting a run at the day boundary would give two half-rows, each with the wrong start and the wrong length, that nothing on screen could put back together.

The measurement behind the day-by-day split does not apply: its worry was twelve aggregate queries a day over a month, while the list asks four aggregate queries for the whole span, and a week of Sessions came back in 0.08 seconds.
The list's queries grow with the number of Sessions and Prompts in the span, not with the number of events, so a busy run never cuts it short.
Reading the list day by day was rejected, because of the midnight cut.
Sending a row at a time was rejected, because the rows are known together from totals over the whole span, so it would add lines without putting anything on screen sooner.

One plain JSON answer outside the Arriving transport was rejected, because the screen still needs to know whether the answer fell short, and a second shape for the same question would be two things to read.

A later correction says the list now asks nine queries, up to eleven with a Repository or Skill filter, plus a tenth to the Trace store for Depth, and the 0.08 second week was measured against the four-query list.
A later record replaces the one-page answer with a gate and its Measures, while the midnight rule is not replaced and the later record rests on it.

The read of the whole span is replaced by the record in which the list reads newest activity first, fifty rows at a time, with no span and no column sort, because Loki refused the totals of a week of Sessions, and the midnight rule stands.
